meta.title: Top 100 Online Fitness Coaches 2026
meta.subtitle: The best coaches you can actually hire on the internet — ranked. Evidence-based physique coaches, transformation PTs, endurance coaches, and the podcasts and creators with real coaching arms.

scoreModel.name: Coaching Influence Score
scoreModel.gate: One hard gate: everyone on this list sells real coaching — 1:1 online coaching, coached programs with feedback, or a coaching app they author. Podcasters and content creators qualify only through a genuine coaching arm.
scoreModel.notes: Reach is log-scaled and platform-weighted, recomputed from researched follower counts. The five judgment factors — coaching, content, credibility, business, engagement — are calibrated across research segments so no category is scored on an easier curve. Counts marked verified were browser-checked at the listed date; the rest are approximate.

meta.disclaimer: Details are editorial estimates (2026) and the ranking is reviewed monthly. Inclusion is not an endorsement and scores measure influence and coaching footprint, not results guarantees — vet any coach before you pay.

entries.name: Renaissance Periodization (Dr. Mike Israetel)
entries.who: Sport scientist (PhD) and RP co-founder; sells the RP Hypertrophy/Strength coaching apps plus direct 1:1 coaching.
entries.why: One of the largest science-based coaching operations in fitness, backed by real academic credentials and a scaled subscription coaching-app business.
entries.takeaway: Turn your training philosophy into a scalable coaching app — a system, not just personal attention.

entries.name: Kayla Itsines
entries.who: Co-founder of Sweat, the global women's fitness app built on her BBG program; sells subscription-based coached training plans across strength, cardio, and postpartum tracks.
entries.why: Built and scaled the largest women's fitness app in the world, reaching over 30 million subscribers; sold Sweat for a nine-figure sum and later reacquired the business.
entries.takeaway: Build one signature program, then scale it into a subscription app — the program is the business.

entries.name: Hany Rambod
entries.who: Creator of FST-7 training; preps IFBB pros and sells the FST-7 training app plus Evogen Nutrition coaching content to the public.
entries.why: Clients have combined for 25 Olympia titles — the deepest documented pro-physique coaching pedigree in this segment.
entries.takeaway: Name your method — a branded system like FST-7 travels further than generic advice.

entries.name: Layne Norton (Carbon Diet Coach / Biolayne)
entries.who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences and natural bodybuilder; co-founded Carbon Diet Coach, an adaptive AI nutrition-coaching app, after moving away from 1:1 coaching.
entries.why: Built one of the first algorithm-driven science-based nutrition coaching products with a strong published-research background.
entries.takeaway: Let an algorithm carry the coaching load once you can't scale 1:1 personally anymore.

entries.name: Joe Wicks
entries.who: UK's 'Body Coach'; sells The Body Coach subscription app (workout + meal plans), the coaching product behind a household fitness brand.
entries.why: Mass-market UK fitness figure — app has passed 1M downloads and generated over £24M; largest reach in this segment.
entries.takeaway: Bundle workouts and meal plans into one subscription — convenience sells wider than either alone.

entries.name: Barbell Medicine
entries.who: Jordan Feigenbaum, MD and Austin Baraki, MD host the Barbell Medicine Podcast; the pair's clinic sells 1:1 coaching in fitness, nutrition, and injury/rehab plus group programming.
entries.why: Physician-led team of 15+ named coaches gives a rare combo of medical credibility and a real individualized coaching business behind the show.
entries.takeaway: Pair medical credentials with a named coaching team — credibility plus real capacity to serve clients.

entries.name: Nick Bare
entries.who: Founder of Bare Performance Nutrition (BPN) and a hybrid-athlete training app/platform (BPN Training, plus a program on Playbook) selling structured run-plus-strength programming.
entries.why: One of the largest hybrid-athlete followings, built on years of documented Ironman, ultra, and military-style training vlogs; the app scales his programming to a large paying audience.
entries.reach: IG ~700K approx · YT ~1.3M approx (not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Document your own training journey publicly — years of vlogged proof becomes the app's marketing.

entries.name: Ben Bergeron
entries.who: Founder of CompTrain and CrossFit New England; sells CompTrain gym and individual-athlete programming (app plus subscriptions).
entries.why: Documented elite client results (2x CrossFit Games champion Katrin Davidsdottir, 10x Games athlete Cole Sager) on top of a real, scaled subscription coaching business.
entries.takeaway: Let your top athletes' results speak — documented champions are the best sales page you have.

entries.name: Legion Athletics / Muscle for Life (Mike Matthews)
entries.who: Mike Matthews hosts the long-running Muscle for Life podcast and runs Legion's 1:1 body-transformation coaching: custom plans, weekly check-in calls, and video form review.
entries.why: Documented scale (Legion claims 5,010+ coaching clients, 91% reporting goal success) backed by weekly-check-in coaching, not just templated plans.
entries.reach: Podcast top health-charts regular · IG ~350K approx (unverified 2026-08)
entries.takeaway: Weekly check-in calls and video form review beat a template — real feedback loops keep clients.

entries.name: Eric Helms (3D Muscle Journey)
entries.who: PhD sport scientist, WNBF pro bodybuilder, and Chief Science Officer/co-founder of 3D Muscle Journey, which sells 1:1 coaching for natural bodybuilders and powerlifters.
entries.why: Elite academic pedigree (research fellow, PhD mentor) paired with a small, well-regarded boutique coaching team.
entries.takeaway: Stay small and boutique on purpose — a tight, credentialed team can outweigh sheer size.

entries.name: Ulisses Jr
entries.who: Natural-bodybuilding coach who runs Ulisses World, an online muscle-building academy enrolling clients from 60+ countries.
entries.why: 25+ years of training experience turned into a large-scale international coaching academy backed by a major supplement sponsorship.
entries.takeaway: Turn decades of hands-on experience into a structured academy that scales past your own client list.

entries.name: Bret Contreras
entries.who: PhD biomechanist known as 'The Glute Guy' who sells Booty by Bret, an online strength program for women built from his own client programming.
entries.why: Inventor of the barbell hip thrust and one of the most credentialed glute-training researchers; his program uses the same workouts he runs with real clients.
entries.takeaway: Sell the exact program you run with real clients — don't water down what actually works.

entries.name: Ben Pakulski
entries.who: IFBB pro bodybuilder running MI40/MI40 Nation, a scaled online muscle-building coaching program and trainer-certification business.
entries.why: Blends elite competitive record with a genuinely large scientific-bodybuilding coaching operation, not just content.
entries.takeaway: Certify other trainers in your method — teaching the teachers multiplies your coaching reach.

entries.name: Jason Koop
entries.who: Head Ultrarunning Coach and Coaching Director at CTS (Carmichael Training Systems); coaches a roster of world-class ultrarunners including Katie Schide.
entries.why: A documented roster of world-class ultrarunning results inside an established, large coaching organization.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled small-mid
entries.takeaway: Coach inside an established organization — infrastructure lets you focus purely on athlete results.

entries.name: James Smith
entries.who: British influencer and content-first coach who built James Smith Academy, an online platform with a team of coaches delivering personalized training plans and accountability.
entries.why: Mega-reach myth-busting content funnels into a genuine coaching business run by a full coaching team, not just him.
entries.takeaway: Use myth-busting content to funnel attention into a real coaching team, not just clicks.

entries.name: Stefi Cohen
entries.who: Doctor of physical therapy, world-record powerlifter, and co-founder of Hybrid Performance Method (HPM), a large team-based online coaching business.
entries.why: Elite competitive record (multiple all-time world records) paired with a scaled coaching team; a rare combination of athletic and clinical credibility.
entries.reach: IG ~1.5M (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Combine clinical training with athletic proof — credentials and competition results reinforce each other.

entries.name: Jordan Syatt
entries.who: World-champion powerlifter and Westside Barbell-certified coach selling Syatt Fitness online barbell and nutrition coaching.
entries.why: Rare combination of elite competitive record, a long-running individualized coaching practice, and comedic/educational content that built a large following.
entries.takeaway: Use humor to teach — comedic, educational content builds trust faster than dry instruction.

entries.name: Krissy Cela
entries.who: Co-founder and lead trainer of EvolveYou (formerly Tone and Sculpt), a strength-training coaching app with structured, personalized programs.
entries.why: Turned a personal-training background into one of the UK's top women's fitness apps, staying hands-on as lead trainer.
entries.takeaway: Stay hands-on as lead trainer even after scaling — presence keeps the product credible.

entries.name: Marcus Filly
entries.who: Founder of Functional Bodybuilding; sells the Persist coaching app, with 10,000+ active paying members across 80+ countries on structured hybrid strength/conditioning tracks.
entries.why: A real, scaled global membership-coaching business rather than templated PDFs, with a large and loyal functional-fitness following.
entries.takeaway: Build ongoing membership coaching, not one-off PDFs — recurring structure builds a loyal following.

entries.name: Jack Daniels
entries.who: Exercise physiologist and Olympic-caliber coach whose VDOT methodology powers the V.O2 (VDOT O2) app, which sells custom training plans and connects athletes to certified coaches.
entries.why: PhD-level exercise science plus a real commercial coaching app make him the credibility anchor for the whole running-coach category.
entries.reach: app-based reach; follower count not independently verified this session
entries.takeaway: Codify your methodology into a formula others can apply — a system outlives any single coach.

entries.name: Squat University (Dr. Aaron Horschig)
entries.who: Dr. Aaron Horschig, DPT, hosts the Squat University podcast and runs a namesake coaching program bridging physical therapy and strength coaching.
entries.why: A licensed doctor of physical therapy running an actual clinical/coaching program gives rare credibility on top of a large following.
entries.takeaway: Bridge physical therapy and strength coaching — treating injuries and building strength in one practice.

entries.name: Natacha Oceane
entries.who: Biophysicist and trainer who sells structured strength/endurance programs, including HYBRID, through the Aflete coaching app.
entries.why: Rare combination of academic rigor (UCL biophysics, Team GB-linked programming) and a genuine coaching product; content is trusted for scientific accuracy.
entries.takeaway: Let your academic background back every claim — accuracy is the trust that sells the program.

entries.name: Meg Squats (Meg Gallagher)
entries.who: Strength and conditioning coach, founder of Stronger by the Day, a membership lifting program and coaching collective for women.
entries.why: Has personally coached tens of thousands of strength athletes from their first squat to national-level meets; long-running, community-driven coaching brand rather than a passive content feed.
entries.takeaway: Build a community members grow inside — from first squat to competition, not a passive feed.

entries.name: Matt Fitzgerald
entries.who: Co-founder of 80/20 Endurance, which has sold 125,000+ training plans and offers certified 1:1 coaching for runners and triathletes on the 80/20 intensity-distribution method.
entries.why: A large-scale coaching-plan business built on a well-documented, science-backed training methodology, plus a prolific authoring record.
entries.reach: IG (personal) 13K (verified 2026-08); 80/20 Endurance brand account larger, not separately verified
entries.takeaway: Publish the science behind your method — a well-documented methodology sells plans at scale.

entries.name: Menno Henselmans
entries.who: Physique scientist and former statistician; sells 1:1 online bodybuilding coaching under his own name (rebranded from Bayesian Bodybuilding).
entries.why: One of the original pioneers of a formally 'evidence-based' individualized coaching method, with peer-reviewed co-authorship.
entries.reach: IG approx 150K (follower count not independently confirmed this pass)
entries.takeaway: Ground every coaching decision in individualized data — evidence-based means adapted to the person, not generic.

entries.name: Greg Nuckols (Stronger by Science)
entries.who: Elite raw powerlifter and researcher; Stronger by Science sells premium 1:1 training and nutrition coaching from its own vetted coaches (e.g., Milo Wolf, Eric Trexler), on top of its free research writing.
entries.why: One of the most respected research-to-practice media brands in fitness, with a real coaching bench behind the newsletter and podcast.
entries.reach: Audience size not independently confirmed this pass (large newsletter/podcast following)
entries.takeaway: Give away the research for free, then sell the vetted coaching bench behind it.

entries.name: Meggan Grubb
entries.who: Australian trainer and founder of the Beyond app, delivering coached training, nutrition, and mindset programs for women at every life stage.
entries.why: Scaled a wellness app to 100,000+ members with a 4.8-star rating, centered on pregnancy and postpartum fitness.
entries.takeaway: Own a specific life stage — pregnancy and postpartum focus built loyalty a generic app can't.

entries.name: Cassey Ho (Blogilates)
entries.who: Founder of Blogilates and its companion training app, plus POPFLEX activewear; sells structured Pilates-based workout programs and calendars.
entries.why: Built one of the largest women's fitness media-and-coaching businesses from POP Pilates, with a decade-plus, highly engaged following.
entries.reach: YT 5.9M · IG 2M+ (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Stay consistent for a decade — a single format repeated builds a loyal, decade-long following.

entries.name: Don Saladino
entries.who: Celebrity strength coach (Ryan Reynolds, Blake Lively, Sebastian Stan) selling the Don Saladino app with tiered strength programs.
entries.why: Consistent superhero-body client roster plus an app used in 100+ countries; also hosts the Stronger with Don Saladino podcast.
entries.takeaway: Package celebrity-client results into tiered programs anyone can buy, not just a select few.

entries.name: Charles Glass
entries.who: Veteran pro-bodybuilding coach who has prepped multiple Mr. Olympia-era champions; sells online coaching and a training-vault app.
entries.why: Among the most respected names in bodybuilding coaching pedigree, still active coaching pros and the public.
entries.takeaway: Stay active coaching both pros and the public — reputation compounds when you never stop coaching.

entries.name: Magnus Lygdback
entries.who: Swedish trainer to A-list actors and musicians; sells the Magnus Method training app with celebrity-style programs.
entries.why: Two decades coaching Ben Affleck, Gal Gadot, Alicia Vikander and others for film roles, now packaged into a consumer app.
entries.takeaway: Package the exact prep you use for elite clients into a consumer product anyone can buy.

entries.name: Kassem Hanson
entries.who: Founder of N1 Training/Education; sells individualized programming courses for trainers and physique-athlete coaching programs.
entries.why: Respected technical voice on exercise selection and individualization, with a scaled education-plus-coaching business.
entries.takeaway: Teach individualization itself — exercise selection principles scale better than one fixed program.

entries.name: Kris Gethin
entries.who: Former Bodybuilding.com head coach; sells extreme-transformation programs through the Kris Gethin Trains app.
entries.why: Built his brand on documented, filmed personal transformations before scaling into a broad online coaching app.
entries.takeaway: Film your own extreme transformation first — proof of personal results precedes the coaching sale.

entries.name: Eugene Teo (Ganbaru Method)
entries.who: Strength coach and content creator; founder of the Ganbaru Method app, which sells customized hybrid-training coaching programs with a coaching team.
entries.why: Fast-growing paid coaching-app audience (200K+ claimed app users) built on a hybrid strength/bodybuilding method.
entries.takeaway: Blend two disciplines into one named method — hybrid strength-and-bodybuilding drew a fast-growing paid audience.

entries.name: Jeff Nippard
entries.who: YouTube science communicator and natural bodybuilder; sells structured, self-guided training programs (hypertrophy, powerbuilding) via jeffnippard.com — no personalized feedback or check-ins.
entries.why: Reference-standard educational content and massive reach; coaching product is templated-only, so it clears the gate but sits at the bottom of the coaching-depth scale.
entries.takeaway: Content can carry a business alone — a templated program still sells if the education is trusted.

entries.name: Jillian Michaels
entries.who: Biggest Loser trainer; sells the award-winning Jillian Michaels Fitness App with structured programs and meal plans.
entries.why: Long-running mainstream celebrity-trainer brand with a genuine app business, not just legacy DVD fame.
entries.takeaway: Keep updating the product behind an old brand — legacy fame only pays if it's still current.

entries.name: Joe Bennett (Hypertrophy Coach)
entries.who: Physique coach behind the Hypertrophy Coach app, selling structured muscle-building programs and coaching to lifters and athletes.
entries.why: Strong reputation for evidence-informed hypertrophy programming packaged into a scaled coaching app.
entries.takeaway: Specialize in one outcome — hypertrophy only — and package that expertise into a focused app.

entries.name: David and Megan Roche
entries.who: Husband-wife coaching duo running SWAP (Some Work, All Play), a coaching business for trail, ultra, and obstacle-course athletes, alongside a weekly podcast.
entries.why: Megan's elite competitive record (national trail champion, Team USA) and documented client results across trail, ultra, and OCR give this a genuine individualized-coaching pedigree.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled mid-size podcast/social audience
entries.takeaway: Coach as a pair — combined competitive credibility and shared workload cover more ground.

entries.name: Floris Gierman
entries.who: Founder of the Personal Best (PB) Program and host of The Extramilest Show; sells heart-rate-based 1:1 and group running coaching.
entries.why: A real coaching business with thousands of documented athlete results, from first 5Ks to Boston qualifiers, built on a large podcast/YouTube audience.
entries.takeaway: Track results across the full range — first 5K to Boston qualifier — and publish the documented range.

entries.name: Mike Tuchscherer (Reactive Training Systems)
entries.who: Founder of Reactive Training Systems (RTS); sells RPE-based autoregulated online coaching for powerlifters.
entries.why: Early pioneer of online powerlifting coaching, with 400+ lifters coached and multiple IPF world-record holders on his roster.
entries.takeaway: Autoregulate by feel, not just fixed numbers — RPE-based coaching adapts to the lifter's actual day.

entries.name: Sohee Lee (Sohee Fit)
entries.who: PhD in Sports Science, CSCS; founder and head coach at SoheeFit Systems, running paid 1:1 online coaching since 2012.
entries.why: Long-running, credentialed coaching practice with a strong, engaged female-focused audience.
entries.takeaway: Stay in the coaching seat for over a decade — longevity itself becomes the credential.

entries.name: Leandro Twin
entries.who: Brazilian physical-education specialist running a personal online/in-person 'assessoria' (coaching consultancy) with custom diet and training plans and biweekly follow-ups.
entries.why: Two decades of bodybuilding/nutrition authority in the Brazilian market, with a hands-on consultancy he personally attends rather than a resold template.
entries.takeaway: Personally attend every consultancy client — biweekly follow-ups beat a plan sold once and forgotten.

entries.name: Caroline Girvan
entries.who: Personal trainer and nutritionist behind the free EPIC YouTube programs and the paid CGX app, which sells structured strength programming and nutrition guidance.
entries.why: One of the most-watched home-workout program creators for women, with a dedicated coaching app extending her free YouTube series into paid, ongoing programming.
entries.takeaway: Give the workout away free on YouTube, then sell the ongoing structure and progression as the app.

entries.name: Senada Greca
entries.who: Founder of WeRise, an all-in-one women's fitness and wellness app covering strength, Pilates, yoga, nutrition, and cycle-syncing.
entries.why: Built one of the most-downloaded women's fitness apps in 2026 off a large, highly engaged personal following.
entries.takeaway: Cover the whole picture in one app — strength, nutrition, and cycle-syncing together, not separate products.

entries.name: Kelsey Wells
entries.who: Sweat global trainer and creator of PWR, a weight-training program for women delivered through the Sweat app.
entries.why: PWR ranked among Sweat's top three most-downloaded training guides in 2026; built a large following around strength training for women specifically.
entries.takeaway: Own a niche inside a bigger platform — strength training for women became its own top-ranked lane.

entries.name: Cliff Wilson
entries.who: Natural pro bodybuilder offering online coaching and contest prep to natural bodybuilding clients.
entries.why: One of the most visible natural-pro coaches, with a large following built on transparent, drug-tested competing.
entries.takeaway: Compete transparently and drug-tested — visible honesty about your own status builds coaching trust.

entries.name: Zach Bitter
entries.who: World-record ultramarathoner who sells personalized ultramarathon coaching (5K to 200+ miles) and group coaching programs via TrainingPeaks.
entries.why: Elite competitive record (100-mile world best, national titles) lends strong credibility to a genuine, individualized coaching business.
entries.takeaway: Coach the full distance range you've raced yourself — 5K to 200 miles, all personally tested.

entries.name: Greg McMillan
entries.who: Exercise scientist and founder of McMillan Running, which sells custom training plans and 1:1 coaching for runners of all levels.
entries.why: One of the longest-running, most respected personalized running-coaching services, grounded in real exercise-science credentials.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled mid-size
entries.takeaway: Ground personalized plans in real exercise science — respected longevity comes from getting the basics right.

entries.name: Ben Carpenter
entries.who: UK personal trainer and author of 'Everything Fat Loss' who sells online personal training and coaching packages.
entries.why: Known for evidence-based, myth-debunking content layered on top of a real solo coaching practice.
entries.takeaway: Debunk myths publicly, then back it with a real, solo coaching practice that proves the point.

entries.name: Hattie Boydle
entries.who: UK powerlifting/bodybuilding champion and coach running Flex Method, a team-coached program on strength, food relationship, and lifting confidence for women.
entries.why: Competitive pedigree (2x world champion) paired with a genuinely coached client program, not just content.
entries.takeaway: Address the food relationship and confidence, not just the lifts — coach the whole person.

entries.name: Revive Stronger (Steve Hall)
entries.who: Steve Hall hosts the Revive Stronger Podcast; Revive Stronger sells online physique coaching with tailored programs and video check-ins, run by a small coaching team.
entries.why: Coaching is genuinely evidence-based and personally delivered, and Hall backs it with his own WNBF pro card (2024) as a natural bodybuilder.
entries.takeaway: Earn your own pro card while you coach — walking the walk backs the evidence-based claims.

entries.name: Sigma Nutrition (Danny Lennon)
entries.who: Danny Lennon hosts Sigma Nutrition Radio; Sigma Nutrition's coaching team of four works directly with pro MMA fighters, boxers, and powerlifters on nutrition.
entries.why: Niche but credible: real paying coaching page, a genuine coach team, and clients who are verifiable competitive athletes.
entries.takeaway: Go niche and credible — a small team serving verifiable pro athletes beats broad, unproven reach.

entries.name: Mind Pump Media
entries.who: Sal Di Stefano, Adam Schafer, and Justin Andrews host the Mind Pump podcast; they sell MAPS training programs and a trainer-facing coaching certification course.
entries.why: One of the biggest fitness podcasts for a decade; the coaching product is real but leans templated (MAPS programs) rather than deeply individualized.
entries.takeaway: Certify trainers in your system — teaching the method scales further than templated programs alone.

entries.name: Anna Engelschall (growingannanas)
entries.who: Certified trainer and former CrossFit coach who founded Grow With Anna, an app with personalized strength, HIIT, and full-body training plans; CEO of The Grow Lifestyle GmbH.
entries.why: One of the largest women's home-workout YouTube channels, converted into a dedicated coaching-app business.
entries.takeaway: Convert your YouTube audience into a paid app — the channel proves demand before you build.

entries.name: Alan Aragon
entries.who: Nutrition researcher and educator (30+ years); runs 1:1 nutrition consulting alongside publishing Alan Aragon's Research Review (AARR).
entries.why: The longest-running evidence-based nutrition research review in fitness, paired with a genuine individual consulting practice.
entries.takeaway: Publish a research review for decades — longevity in honest analysis outlasts any single trend.

entries.name: Diren Kartal
entries.who: Turkish-British coach offering 1:1 'Confidence Coaching' and the group program Progress247, built on over a decade of gym-floor coaching experience.
entries.why: Claims 40,000+ people coached online, with a non-restrictive, sustainability-first approach that built strong cross-market (English + Turkish) reach.
entries.takeaway: Make sustainability the pitch, not restriction — a non-restrictive approach keeps clients coming back.

entries.name: Danny Matranga (Dynamic Dialogue)
entries.who: Danny Matranga hosts the 400+ episode Dynamic Dialogue podcast; sells app-based training plus 1:1 coaching with Coach Danny and his coaching team.
entries.why: Combines a consistent twice-weekly educational show with a real named coaching team, not just a self-serve app.
entries.takeaway: Show up twice a week, every week — consistency in a long-running show builds the audience that buys.

entries.name: Chloe Ting
entries.who: YouTube workout-challenge creator whose paid Chloe Ting app turns her free challenge format into a subscription coaching product.
entries.why: Enormous global reach; passes the gate narrowly on the authored coaching app rather than the free YouTube challenges.
entries.takeaway: Turn your free viral challenge format into a paid, ongoing subscription once the audience is proven.

entries.name: Simeon Panda
entries.who: UK bodybuilder-influencer selling online training programs (Mass Gain Extreme, Fat Burn Extreme, Toned and Sexy) through simeonpanda.com.
entries.why: One of the largest bodybuilding-adjacent reach numbers in the segment, monetized across apparel, supplements, and coaching programs.
entries.takeaway: Monetize the same audience across apparel, supplements, and coaching — one following, several revenue lines.

entries.name: Paul Revelia
entries.who: Pro Physique competitor and YouTuber selling online contest-prep and physique coaching to amateur competitors.
entries.why: Documentary-style prep content built real coaching-client demand from the physique-competitor audience.
entries.takeaway: Film your own contest prep like a documentary — that transparency is what pulls in coaching clients.

entries.name: Kim French
entries.who: UK personal trainer behind the Believe by Kim French app, selling 40+ coached home/gym plans with macro-based nutrition guidance and progress tracking.
entries.why: Runs one of the higher-grossing women's fitness apps in the 'busy mum' niche, with strong app-store ratings and a loyal repeat-subscriber base.
entries.takeaway: Design specifically for the time-crunched — a clear niche like busy mums earns loyal repeat subscribers.

entries.name: Harley Pasternak
entries.who: Celebrity trainer (Halle Berry, Ariana Grande, Rihanna) selling the 5-Factor coaching methodology through books and online programs.
entries.why: Nutrition-science credentials plus a decades-deep celebrity roster distinguish him from pure influencer trainers.
entries.takeaway: Back your method with nutrition science, not just celebrity photos — credentials separate you from influencers.

entries.name: Milos Sarcev
entries.who: Veteran IFBB pro coach ('Mind Sculpting') who has trained multiple Olympia-level competitors and coaches the public online.
entries.why: Old-school bodybuilding coaching pedigree with a client list spanning multiple eras of pro bodybuilding.
entries.takeaway: Coach across eras without going stale — decades of relevance beats one moment of fame.

entries.name: Stan Efferding
entries.who: Elite powerlifter and bodybuilder behind the Vertical Diet, selling online nutrition/training consulting to strength and physique athletes.
entries.why: Rare combination of elite competitive record in two sports with a real consulting practice built on it.
entries.takeaway: Name your nutrition approach clearly — a branded diet concept like Vertical Diet is easier to sell.

entries.name: Taren Gesell
entries.who: YouTuber ('Triathlon Taren') and founder/CEO of MOTTIV, a triathlon and marathon training app selling structured coached plans and virtual coaching.
entries.why: Built a real subscription coaching-app business on top of one of the largest triathlon content channels aimed at everyday age-groupers.
entries.reach: IG 57K (verified 2026-08); YouTube subscriber count not verified this session (larger, approx)
entries.takeaway: Target the everyday age-grouper, not just elites — the biggest audience is the amateur majority.

entries.name: Courteney Fisher
entries.who: US fitness and Pilates coach behind 'Fit With Coco,' a patented 3-2-1 strength-and-Pilates method sold as ongoing programs and challenges.
entries.why: Viral 3-2-1 workout format converted into a real, repeat-purchase coaching platform, not just a one-off trend.
entries.takeaway: Turn a viral moment into a repeat-purchase platform — don't let a trend end as a one-off.

entries.name: Jono Castano
entries.who: Sydney-based trainer and founder of Acero, whose Acero Drip app sells 24/7 coaching access, workout programs, and a members' community.
entries.why: Built a recognizable training brand (Acero) and converted it into an app-based coaching subscription business.
entries.takeaway: Offer 24/7 access and a community, not just workouts — availability and belonging drive subscriptions.

entries.name: Renato Cariani
entries.who: Brazilian pro bodybuilder running a personalized 'consultoria' offering individualized training, nutrition, and monitoring, plus a new physical training center opening in 2026.
entries.why: One of the largest reach numbers in the segment worldwide, backed by a real paid consultancy and a bricks-and-mortar training-center expansion.
entries.takeaway: Expand from online consultancy into a physical training center — reach and real estate reinforce each other.

entries.name: Nerd Fitness (Steve Kamb)
entries.who: Steve Kamb built Nerd Fitness into a long-running fitness media brand (blog, newsletter, YouTube); Nerd Fitness Coaching pairs clients with real human coaches for multiple weekly check-ins and video form review.
entries.why: One of the oldest continuously-running online coaching operations in the space (since 2009), with a genuinely documented human check-in process, not just an app.
entries.takeaway: Keep a human check-in process running for over a decade — longevity beats novelty in coaching.

entries.name: Brianna Battles
entries.who: Founder of the Pregnancy & Postpartum Athleticism Coalition (PPAC), running coaching and certification programs for pre/postnatal athletes and the coaches who train them.
entries.why: Leading voice in pre/postnatal return-to-training coaching, widely cited among strength and CrossFit coaches for a rigorous, athlete-specific framework.
entries.reach: IG ~150K (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Build a rigorous framework for an underserved population, then certify other coaches to deliver it.

entries.name: Gunnar Peterson
entries.who: Longtime celebrity trainer (Kardashian-Jenner family, pro athletes) offering online training programs through his own site.
entries.why: One of the longest-running names in celebrity training, with continued reach through A-list clients.
entries.takeaway: Stay relevant across decades by continually training the current generation of high-profile clients.

entries.name: Rich Ryan
entries.who: Pro trail/ultra runner who runs Reinforced Running, a 1:1 and group online coaching service for trail and ultra athletes.
entries.why: Elite competitive trail-running credentials paired with an active, individualized coaching roster and instructive YouTube content.
entries.reach: IG ~40K approx (not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Teach through instructive YouTube content while running an active, individualized coaching roster alongside it.

entries.name: Hunter Allen
entries.who: Co-creator of the power-based cycling training methodology behind TrainingPeaks and founder of Peaks Coaching Group, a team cycling-coaching business.
entries.why: A decades-long, well-established cycling coaching operation with a real team of coaches and a foundational power-training book.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled small
entries.takeaway: Write the foundational book on your method — a text that defines the field outlasts any single client.

entries.name: Renato Canova
entries.who: Elite distance-running coach who provides individualized 1:1 coaching to professional marathoners and distance runners, largely East African elites.
entries.why: Widely credited with coaching multiple world-record and championship-level marathoners; the deepest competitive-pedigree credibility anchor in this segment, even without a consumer-facing coaching product.
entries.reach: no public social following tracked; elite-coaching reach only, approx-labeled
entries.takeaway: You don't need a consumer product — pure results with elite athletes can be the whole reputation.

entries.name: Paul Carter (Lift-Run-Bang)
entries.who: Bodybuilder/powerlifter with nearly 30 years in the field; founder of Lift-Run-Bang, an online coaching platform that has trained thousands of athletes.
entries.why: Long track record coaching a large client base with a pragmatic, research-informed hypertrophy approach.
entries.takeaway: Stay pragmatic — a research-informed but practical hypertrophy approach keeps thousands of clients training long-term.

entries.name: Andrew Coates (Andrew Coates Fitness)
entries.who: Coach with 23,000+ logged coaching hours; sells exclusive 1:1 online coaching with daily check-ins, program design, and nutrition guidance.
entries.why: Deep hands-on coaching volume paired with a respected evidence-based industry podcast on the side.
entries.takeaway: Log the hours — daily check-ins and deep hands-on coaching volume are what actually build the reputation.

entries.name: Alexia Clark
entries.who: 'Queen of Workouts' and founder of the Alexia Clark app, which sells weekly workouts, a nutrition plan, and direct personal support from Alexia.
entries.why: Built a large, loyal 'QueenTeam' community and a subscription coaching app with genuine 1:1 access, not just templated content.
entries.takeaway: Give the community a name and direct personal access — a loyal 'team' identity keeps subscribers renewing.

entries.name: Linn Lowes
entries.who: Swedish fitness entrepreneur and cancer survivor who founded the Athli App, offering customizable gym and home workout programs plus nutrition plans.
entries.why: Converted a large personal following into a self-built coaching platform with over 20 workout programs and thousands of recipes.
entries.takeaway: Convert a personal story and following into a self-built platform, not someone else's white-label app.

entries.name: Dylan Johnson
entries.who: Pro cyclist and YouTuber who co-founded Ignition Coaching Co, which sells 1:1 cycling coaching.
entries.why: Combines a genuinely instructive, science-based YouTube channel with a real coaching business he co-founded and operates.
entries.reach: IG 76K (verified 2026-08); YouTube subscriber count not verified this session
entries.takeaway: Operate the coaching business you co-founded yourself — don't just license your name to it.

entries.name: Milo Wolf (Wolf Coaching / Stronger by Science)
entries.who: PhD candidate in sport science and competitive natural bodybuilder; coaches clients through Wolf Coaching and as a Stronger by Science coach.
entries.why: Active hypertrophy researcher (range-of-motion, lengthened partials) whose own findings feed directly into a real coaching practice.
entries.reach: IG (@wolfcoach_) follower count not independently confirmed this pass, approx sub-100K
entries.takeaway: Feed your own research findings directly into your coaching practice — test theory on real clients.

entries.name: Emily Skye
entries.who: Founder of the Emily Skye FIT app, selling structured strength and postpartum-inclusive training programs for women.
entries.why: One of the earliest fitness-app founders in this space, with a large, long-standing global following built well before the current wave of coaching apps.
entries.reach: IG ~2.8M (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Move early into app-based coaching — being first in a niche builds a following that lasts.

entries.name: Chris Aceto
entries.who: Longtime pro-bodybuilding contest-prep coach and nutrition consultant selling 1:1 online prep coaching.
entries.why: Decades of documented contest-prep results with top-level competitors; niche but deeply credentialed.
entries.takeaway: Stay deeply niche on purpose — decades of documented results in one lane beat broad, shallow reach.

entries.name: Fergus Crawley
entries.who: Hybrid athlete and co-founder/head coach of Omnia Performance, a coaching brand for concurrent (strength-plus-endurance) training.
entries.why: Runs a real hybrid-training coaching business and market-tests his own methodology through extreme, well-documented endurance feats.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled
entries.takeaway: Test your own methodology through extreme, documented feats before selling it to clients.

entries.name: Chris Hinshaw
entries.who: Founder of Aerobic Capacity; sells endurance-conditioning coaching and programming used by numerous CrossFit Games athletes and gyms.
entries.why: Widely credited as the go-to aerobic-capacity coach inside competitive CrossFit and Hyrox-adjacent functional fitness, with documented Games-level client results.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled small
entries.takeaway: Specialize in the one weakness everyone in your sport shares — aerobic capacity was the gap he owned.

entries.name: Alex Crockford
entries.who: UK trainer and founder of the CrockFit / Alex Crockford app, offering home and gym programs, coaching calls, community access, and fitness retreats.
entries.why: Longest-running app in the set (PDF plans since 2015, app since 2018), with a durable coaching-plus-community model.
entries.takeaway: Add retreats and coaching calls on top of the app — community depth is what makes a model durable.

entries.name: Sophia Thiel
entries.who: German fitness personality selling 'Healthy Inside Out,' a coached 12-week program (with Gymondo) covering kick-start, reshape, and maintenance phases plus 130+ recipes.
entries.why: Germany's best-known women's transformation coach, rebuilt around a mental-health-forward, sustainable-habits program after years in the public eye.
entries.takeaway: Rebuild your program around mental health and sustainable habits, not just a transformation photo.

entries.name: Alex Viada
entries.who: Founder of Complete Human Performance; sells 1:1 hybrid strength-and-endurance coaching and authored 'The Hybrid Athlete.'
entries.why: One of the original authorities on concurrent strength/endurance training, with a long-running individualized coaching business.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled small
entries.takeaway: Write the book that defines your niche before anyone else does — first-mover authority sticks.

entries.name: Bryce Lewis (The Strength Athlete)
entries.who: Elite drug-free powerlifter (USAPL/IPF record holder); founded The Strength Athlete (TSA), an online powerlifting coaching group.
entries.why: Competitive record backs a dedicated, longstanding powerlifting-only coaching business.
entries.takeaway: Stay single-sport — a powerlifting-only coaching group backed by your own competitive record builds trust.

entries.name: Alberto Nunez (Team 3DMJ)
entries.who: WNBF pro natural bodybuilder and Team 3DMJ coach, selling 1:1 natural bodybuilding coaching.
entries.why: Competitive pro pedigree combined with membership in the well-regarded 3DMJ coaching collective.
entries.takeaway: Join a well-regarded coaching collective — a respected team lends credibility no solo brand can buy alone.

entries.name: Trevor Kashey (Trevor Kashey Nutrition)
entries.who: PhD biochemist; founder of Trevor Kashey Nutrition, selling 1:1 'Cognitive Nutrition' coaching to individuals and fitness professionals.
entries.why: PhD-level nutrition science applied through a scaled 1:1 coaching program with a claimed 12,000+ client history.
entries.takeaway: Coach the coaches too — selling to fitness professionals multiplies the reach of your expertise.

entries.name: Emma Storey-Gordon
entries.who: Dundee-based coach running 1:1 online coaching plus two group coaching businesses (including the EC Method) and a separate nutrition-coaching business.
entries.why: Runs several parallel, genuinely coached programs rather than one flagship product, with a recent 600+ client group-coaching intake.
entries.takeaway: Run parallel coaching businesses instead of one flagship product — diversify the offer, not just the audience.

entries.name: Barbell Shrugged / Shrugged Collective
entries.who: Anders Varner and Doug Larson host the long-running Barbell Shrugged podcast; Shrugged Collective sells its Program Vault training programs and, per its own site, now partners with RAPID Health Optimization to coach elite athletes and executives.
entries.why: The RAPID Health Optimization partnership adds a genuine high-end coaching arm on top of what would otherwise be templated program sales.
entries.takeaway: Partner with a specialist coaching brand to add a real coaching arm to your templated products.

entries.name: GDFIT (Greg Doucette)
entries.who: Greg Doucette is one of fitness YouTube's largest personalities; his GDFIT app sells structured, semi-personalized training and nutrition coaching plans.
entries.why: Huge reach and a real coaching app, but the coaching leans templated/algorithmic rather than a human check-in relationship, so it scores at the lower end of the coaching gate.
entries.takeaway: Reach alone isn't coaching — semi-personalized templates still need a real path toward genuine feedback.

entries.name: Massy Arias
entries.who: Personal trainer and mental-health advocate running her own online coaching programs for women.
entries.why: Known for pairing strength coaching with mental-health advocacy, building a highly engaged, mission-driven community rather than a purely aesthetic following.
entries.reach: IG ~1.8M (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Pair strength coaching with mental-health advocacy — a mission-driven community engages deeper than aesthetics.

entries.name: Susan Niebergall
entries.who: Certified personal trainer and strength coach running Susan Niebergall Fitness, a solo online weight-loss coaching practice.
entries.why: Smaller, solo operation but a genuine ongoing coaching relationship rather than a templated program.
entries.takeaway: Stay small and solo if it means an ongoing relationship — genuine coaching beats a bigger templated funnel.

entries.name: Danyele Wilson
entries.who: Tone & Sculpt (EvolveYou) HIIT trainer and founder of the SPARC app, combining workouts with mindset training.
entries.why: Corporate-marketing-turned-fitness-coach whose body-positive coaching and personal story built a devoted, engaged following.
entries.takeaway: Combine workouts with mindset training and tell your own career-change story to build a devoted following.

entries.name: Sage Canaday
entries.who: Professional mountain-ultra-trail runner who sells coaching and training plans through his own site and Higher Running.
entries.why: 20 years of elite trail/ultra racing credibility backing a real, individualized coaching service.
entries.reach: reach not independently verified this session, approx-labeled small
entries.takeaway: Let two decades of elite racing back your individualized coaching — lived experience is the credential.

entries.name: Joe Delaney
entries.who: Irish, Ibiza-based personal trainer selling personal training services and the structured 'Ibiza Shreds' upper/lower hypertrophy program.
entries.why: Built a mid-size following around a genuinely followed, spreadsheet-backed training program plus direct PT sales.
entries.takeaway: Back the program with an actual spreadsheet people can follow — structure sells alongside direct PT.

entries.name: Julian Zietlow
entries.who: German coach and founder of vegan supplement brand Rocka Nutrition, selling the 'Size Zero 2.0' nutrition-and-training concept plus live mentoring sessions.
entries.why: Smaller reach than the segment's leaders, but a real, named coaching concept with high audience engagement.
entries.takeaway: Add live mentoring sessions on top of a named concept — direct access drives engagement past reach.

entries.name: Amanda Bucci
entries.who: Certified nutrition and fitness coach running Bucci Fit, an online 1:1 and group coaching business for women.
entries.why: Solo coach with a thriving, personality-driven brand blending nutrition coaching, business content, and fitness.
entries.reach: IG ~700K (approx, not independently verified this session)
entries.takeaway: Blend business content with fitness coaching — a personality-driven brand can serve more than one interest.

bubblingUnder.name: Lyle McDonald (Bodyrecomposition)
bubblingUnder.who: Longtime evidence-based nutrition/training author; sells paid 60-minute 1:1 online consultations via bodyrecomposition.com rather than ongoing coaching.
bubblingUnder.why: Foundational figure in evidence-based fitness writing; the coaching product is a limited one-off consult, so it barely clears the gate.
bubblingUnder.reach: Reach not independently confirmed this pass (longtime niche following, no active mainstream social presence found)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: A single well-prepared consult can be the whole coaching product — depth over an ongoing retainer.

bubblingUnder.name: Brains and Gains (Dr. David Maconi)
bubblingUnder.who: Dr. David Maconi hosts the Brains and Gains podcast; he sells coaching through his own site and coaches through the Boostcamp app.
bubblingUnder.why: Smallest, most niche pass on this list, but the coaching product is real and named, not just a supplement funnel.

handles.podcast: Brains and Gains with Dr. David Maconi

bubblingUnder.takeaway: Keep the coaching product real and named, even at small scale — never let it become a supplement funnel.
